messages.author: 2a2e2c2381dcfe6a
messages.subject: Spatio-temporal autocorrelation of measurement error
parts:
Hi Chris,


I have a question regarding handling spatio-temporal autocorrelation of measurement errors in ctmm package.

You take into account the autocorrelation of location data in the modeling, I am wondering if it includes autocorrelation of measurement errors as well.

Are HDOP values enough for estimating the autocorrelation of measurement errors in the modeling?

 

Thanks in advance,

Maryam

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Spatio-temporal autocorrelation of measurement error
parts:
Hi Maryam,

We do not yet model error autocorrelation. So far, for sampling down to 10-15 second intervals, I haven't personally seen any autocorrelation in modern GPS telemetry error, but I am about to look at some of new e-obs solar tags that collect 1 second data when the battery is full. I also know from the literature that older GPS data is supposed to have substantial error autocorrelation at under ~30 second intervals.

For the future, when the kind of data that has autocorrelated error is being collected (maybe the new e-obs solar tags?), handling it will require calibration data to be collected. The HDOP values only account for the heteroskedasticity, not the autocorrelation. But, fortunately, the autocorrelation only emerges at very short timescales.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Spatio-temporal autocorrelation of measurement error
parts:
Hi Maryam,

As with most things, you should check your own data. Recent development versions of ctmm on GitHub support the residuals() method on (calibrated) calibration data and you can feed that into the correlogram() method to check for autocorrelation.

But here is a reference on autocorrelation in L1-GPS data where they actually show a plot of the error ACF, which I don't think they standardized by DOP, but shows the autocorrelation dying off in around 50 seconds (Fig. 2).

Tao, Z., and P. Bonnifait. 2015. Modeling L1-GPS errors for an enhanced data fusion with
lane marking maps for road automated vehicles. In European Navigation Conference
(ENC 2015). Bordeaux, France.

I have not yet come across a calibration dataset collected at a higher rate than 5-10 seconds.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: Spatio-temporal autocorrelation of measurement error
parts:
Dear Chris,

I have collected calibration data over 3 hours with the time interval of 10 seconds with the Canmore GT-740FL GPS device. Figure 1 shows the corresponding error autocorrelation plot for my calibration data using residuals() and correlogram() functions.

I subsampled the calibration data to 1 minute time interval and did the same procedure as above-mentioned to check the error autocorrelation of observations with 1 minute time interval.

In Figure 2 unlike Figure 1, a lot of points are within the upper and lower band drawn by the red dotted dash-lines. It means for many time lags, the error autocorrelation are statistically zero . Can I conclude that the impact of error autocorrelation is negligible for observations with 1 minute time interval? If so, What about the specific time lag of 1 minute in Figure 1 and 2? It is statistically non-zero. How can I interpret it?

 

Thank you in advance,

Maryam

messages.subject: Re: Spatio-temporal autocorrelation of measurement error
parts:
Hi Maryam,

The x-axis of Figure 1 looks like 1-minute intervals. Is the data irregular (perhaps with a mix of 10 second and 1 minute intervals?) and have you tried playing with the dt argument?

The first lag (1 minute?) looks to have significant autocorrelation, however if the sampling is irregular that can be an artifact of discretization. You can mitigate this somewhat by increasing the res option in correlogram() or better with fast=FALSE like in the example.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Spatio-temporal autocorrelation of measurement error
parts:
Hi Jakob,

Unfortunately, I have not gotten my hands on entirely genuine calibration data of that nature. What I had access to was a tag on a bird that was supposed to be roosting, so I could not definitely say what was what... and the "errors" seemed suspiciously large to be as smooth/colored as they were. If you have any calibration data of that type, where you leave the tag out in a fixed spot over an extended period of time, I would like to take a look.

My suspicion, though, is that there is some threshold around 30 seconds at which you get normal GPS error autocorrelation and maybe a second threshold at which you get additional error autocorrelation from the device's Kalman filter. As this data becomes common, we will put tools in the package to account for the error autocorrelation, but first I need something to look at and play with.

Best,
Chris
